tier_reason: The independent nativejson-benchmark sample CSV has json-c, Jansson, cJSON, Nlohmann and JsonCpp Stringify/Prettify rows on a Core i7-4980HQ with clang 7.0 64-bit; the harness is public (src/tests/jsonctest.cpp calls json_object_to_json_string_ext with JSON_C_TO_STRING_PLAIN/PRETTY, src/tests/janssontest.cpp etc.) and build/premake5.lua sets release optimize Full, NDEBUG and -march=native, so A holds as for the Jansson and ujson4c entries.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Stringify time, sum of the three files (derived from page data): json-c 30.804 ms (16.260 + 9.990 + 4.554) vs Jansson 69.910 ms (about 2.3x), cJSON 71.283 ms (about 2.3x), Nlohmann 87.732 ms (about 2.8x) and JsonCpp 94.261 ms (about 3.1x); prettify sum 49.256 ms vs Jansson 80.380 ms (about 1.6x) and Nlohmann 130.560 ms (about 2.7x). The whole win comes from canada.json (stringify 16.260 ms vs Jansson 64.221, cJSON 49.510, Nlohmann 76.315, JsonCpp 84.443; prettify 29.737 vs Jansson 73.837, Nlohmann 112.750). On citm_catalog.json and twitter.json json-c is slower than Jansson (stringify 9.990/4.554 ms vs 3.764/1.925 ms; prettify 14.057/5.462 vs 4.373/2.170), Nlohmann (stringify 7.178/4.239) and JsonCpp (stringify 5.679/4.139), and beats only cJSON (15.016/6.757). All ratios derived from page data.
corrections.caveats: The stringify win is confined to canada.json and comes from a parse-time cache: json-c's tokener stores a strdup of every double's original text (json_object_new_double_s, 0.12.1 json_tokener.c line 703, still present at HEAD) and the serializer memcpy's that text back instead of formatting the double, so a DOM built from parsing skips double-to-text conversion while doubles created in code go through snprintf("%.17g"). The cost moves to parsing: json-c's canada.json parse is 105.784 ms with 33.7 MB and 390,651 allocations (Nlohmann 55.591 ms, 5.3 MB). On citm_catalog.json and twitter.json json-c stringifies 2.4-2.7x slower than Jansson and slower than Nlohmann and JsonCpp. Parse time (134.551 ms for the three files) is slower than most libraries in the suite and beats only JsonCpp (165.522 ms), PicoJSON (140.256 ms) and a few others; RapidJSON stringifies the three files in 11.209 ms. Third-party suite by the RapidJSON author (disclosed), numbers from 2016 with json-c 0.12.1, many releases behind the current 0.19. Library versions come from the suite README's table, which was edited after the 2016-09-09 sample run (it lists cJSON 1.5.0, released 2017-05-02), so the exact versions measured are not certain. Conformance in the same suite: 22 of 34 parse-validation, 57 of 66 double-parse, 9 of 9 string and 27 of 27 roundtrip tests. json-c's README makes no benchmark claim. Flags come from the repo's premake file, not from the result file. Output formatting differs between libraries, so serialized bytes are not identical across rows.

notes: Every number matches the CSV, but the summed stringify/prettify win hides that json-c loses to Jansson, Nlohmann and JsonCpp on two of three files; the canada.json win comes from re-emitting each double's original text cached at parse time (json_object_new_double_s). Shortcomings to record: win confined to canada.json via parse-time number-text cache, slow and memory-heavy parse, 2016 data on 0.12.1, README version table postdates the run.

tier_reason: For parsing, the independent nativejson-benchmark sample CSV has udp/json-parser and Nlohmann/Jansson/json-c/JsonCpp '1. Parse' rows on a Core i7-4980HQ with clang 7.0 64-bit; the harness is public (src/tests/udpjsontest.cpp calls json_parse_ex; src/tests/nlohmanntest.cpp) and build/premake5.lua sets release optimize Full, NDEBUG and -march=native, so A holds for the parse claim. The stringify/prettify claim is not valid on canada.json (lossy %g output from udp/json-builder) and is restated on the other two files.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Parse time, sum of the three files (derived from page data): udp/json-parser 47.338 ms (29.536 + 13.058 + 4.744) vs Nlohmann 72.476 ms (55.591 + 9.875 + 7.010), about 1.5x; vs Jansson 112.056 ms about 2.4x, json-c 134.551 ms about 2.8x, JsonCpp 165.522 ms about 3.5x. The win over Nlohmann comes entirely from canada.json (29.536 vs 55.591 ms), the double-heavy file where udp's number parser is not correctly rounded; on citm_catalog.json plus twitter.json udp takes 17.802 ms vs Nlohmann 16.885 ms (about 5% slower), Jansson 33.591 ms (about 1.9x), json-c 28.767 ms (about 1.6x) and JsonCpp 23.064 ms (about 1.3x). Stringify/prettify come from the separate udp/json-builder library, which prints doubles with sprintf("%g") (6 significant digits), so its canada.json rows time lossy output and are not comparable; on citm_catalog.json plus twitter.json (integers and strings, one 0.087) stringify is 2.444 ms vs Nlohmann 11.417 ms (about 4.7x), Jansson 5.689 ms (about 2.3x) and RapidJSON 1.871 ms, prettify 2.797 ms vs Nlohmann 17.810 ms (about 6.4x). All ratios derived from page data.
corrections.workload: nativejson-benchmark: parse in-memory canada.json (2199KB), citm_catalog.json (1737KB) and twitter.json (632KB) into a DOM with udp/json-parser (json_parse_ex, suite README lists 1.1.0, submodule 7053321); stringify and prettify of that DOM use the separate udp/json-builder library (json_measure_ex + json_serialize_ex, submodule 19c739f).
corrections.caveats: Number handling is loose: the parser builds a double as integer part + fraction / pow(10, digits), then multiplies by pow(10, exponent) (same code at the pinned 7053321 and at HEAD), so values are not correctly rounded (37 of 66 double-parse conformance tests pass vs 66 of 66 for Nlohmann), and the parse win over Nlohmann exists only on the double-heavy canada.json; on the other two files it is about 5% slower. Output rows are produced by udp/json-builder, a separate repository, which formats doubles with "%g" (6 significant digits, still so at HEAD): canada.json's 17-digit coordinates are truncated, so those stringify/prettify timings measure lossy output (22 of 27 roundtrip tests pass). The benchmark wrapper's own comment says stringify is 'Very slow in the current version'. Third-party suite by the RapidJSON author (disclosed in its README), sample numbers from 2016-09-09; Library versions come from the suite README's table, which was edited after the 2016-09-09 sample run (it lists cJSON 1.5.0, released 2017-05-02), so the exact versions measured are not certain. Conformance: 26 of 34 parse-validation, 37 of 66 double-parse, 9 of 9 string, 22 of 27 roundtrip (Nlohmann 34/34, 66/66, 9/9, 23/27). RapidJSON parses the three files in 7.932 ms. The project README gives no performance numbers, only design claims (never recurses, allocates only what it needs). September 2026 commits fixed parser correctness edge cases (rejection of long floats #178, overflow handling, UTF-16 surrogate pairs); the benchmark files exercise none of them (canada.json parsed, no \u escapes in citm_catalog.json or twitter.json), so the 2016 numbers are not capped by them. The repository now lives at github.com/json-parser/json-parser (udp/json-parser redirects there). Flags come from the repo's premake file, not from the result file.

notes: Numbers match the CSV, but the stringify/prettify sums include canada.json rows where udp/json-builder emits doubles with %g (6 significant digits), i.e. lossy output, so I restated them on citm+twitter only; the parse win over Nlohmann is confined to canada.json, where udp's doubles are inexactly rounded. Shortcomings to record: lossy %g serializer (json-builder, separate repo) behind the canada output rows, inexact double parsing (37/66), no parse win over Nlohmann outside canada.json, 2016 data. Metadata checked (BSD-2-Clause, 1.3k stars, last commit 2026-09-19); the repo moved to github.com/json-parser/json-parser, so a repo_url override may be worth recording.

tier_reason: The independent nativejson-benchmark sample CSV has Nlohmann (C++11) and JsonCpp/PicoJSON/json-c/Jansson '1. Parse' rows on a Core i7-4980HQ with clang 7.0 64-bit; the harness is public (src/tests/nlohmanntest.cpp, src/tests/jsoncpptest.cpp) and build/premake5.lua sets release optimize Full, NDEBUG and -march=native, so A holds for the parse-vs-JsonCpp claim.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Parse time, sum of the three files (derived from page data): Nlohmann 72.476 ms (55.591 + 9.875 + 7.010) vs JsonCpp 165.522 ms (about 2.3x faster), PicoJSON 140.256 ms (about 1.9x), json-c 134.551 ms (about 1.9x) and Jansson 112.056 ms (about 1.5x). Parse memory sum 9,897,872 bytes vs JsonCpp 24,560,400, Jansson 18,319,600 and json-c 49,886,288 (derived from page data). Stringify sum 87.732 ms is only on par with JsonCpp 94.261 ms.
corrections.caveats: Weak record and a category incumbent: nlohmann/json is one of the json category's named baselines in spec Part 4, and its README says 'There are certainly faster JSON libraries out there'. In the same sample it is mid-pack: RapidJSON parses the three files in 7.932 ms (about 9x faster), cJSON 24.671 ms, udp/json-parser 47.338 ms (all derived from page data), and its prettify sum (130.560 ms) is slower than json-c (49.256 ms), cJSON (71.418 ms) and Jansson (80.380 ms). Numbers are from the 2016-09-09 sample with v2.0.3, long before the 3.x series; Library versions come from the suite README's table, which was edited after the 2016-09-09 sample run (it lists cJSON 1.5.0, released 2017-05-02), so the exact versions measured are not certain. Newer results put it last: stephenberry/json_performance (June 8, 2025, MacBook Pro M1, Clang 17, 1,000,000 iterations; run by the Glaze author, so not independent of a competitor) lists nlohmann at 15.44 s roundtrip, 86 MB/s write, 81 MB/s read, the slowest of the nine libraries in every column, so no current speed advantage is documented. Third-party suite by the RapidJSON author (disclosed). Flags come from the repo's premake file, not the result file.

notes: Numbers match the CSV (only fix: vs Jansson is 1.55x, so about 1.5x, not 1.6x). The project is a json-category incumbent named in spec Part 4 baselines and is slower than most current libraries, so the orchestrator may prefer a duplicate/incumbent decision; if kept, record 'category incumbent, not faster than the category's other baselines, 2016 v2.0.3 data, last in json_performance 2025'.
